51419.e: The stone temples on Malta are over 5000 years old. They are among the oldest free-standing buildings in the world.
51419.m: Malta’s stone temples are older than the pyramids.

51420.q: Which is the largest island in Germany?
51420.e: Rügen covers almost 1000 square kilometres. This makes it the largest island in Germany.
51420.m: Rügen is the largest island in Germany.

51421.q: Which sea is the island of Rügen in?
51421.e: Rügen lies off the coast in north-eastern Germany. The Baltic Sea is there.
51421.m: Rügen is in the Baltic Sea.

51422.q: What is the coast in Jasmund National Park on Rügen known for?
51422.e: On the coast of Jasmund, steep white chalk cliffs rise out of the sea. The best known is called the Königsstuhl (King’s Chair).
51422.m: Rügen has bright white chalk cliffs.

51423.q: What are the white cliffs on the coast of Rügen made of?
51423.e: The cliffs on Rügen are made of chalk. It formed from the tiny shells of sea creatures.
51423.m: The white cliffs on Rügen are made of chalk.

51424.q: Which country does the island of Rügen belong to?
51424.e: Rügen lies in the Baltic Sea off the coast of north-eastern Germany.

51425.q: How do you get to the island of Rügen by car?
a: Through a tunnel under the sea
On a road across the ice
51425.e: From the town of Stralsund, the Rügen Causeway and the Rügen Bridge lead to the island. That is how cars and trains get across.

51426.q: What powers the old engine of the little “Rasender Roland” railway on Rügen?
51426.e: The “Rasender Roland” (Racing Roland) is a small railway with a steam engine. Despite its name, it runs quite slowly.
51426.m: The Rasender Roland on Rügen runs on steam.

51427.q: How many countries belong to the European Union (as of 2026)?
51427.e: The European Union has 27 member countries. They include, for example, Germany, France, Italy and Austria.
51427.m: The European Union has 27 member countries.

a: The people in the EU countries
The governments of the EU countries
The heads of state of the EU countries
51428.e: Every five years the adults in the EU countries elect the European Parliament.
51428.m: The EU Parliament is elected by the people.

51429.q: Which country left the EU in 2020?
51429.e: Great Britain left the EU on 31 January 2020. This is called “Brexit”.
51429.m: With Brexit, Great Britain left the EU.

51430.q: Which neighbouring country of Switzerland is NOT in the EU?
51430.e: Liechtenstein is not a member of the EU. Germany, France, Italy and Austria are members.
51430.m: Liechtenstein is not part of the EU.

51431.q: Which piece of music is the anthem of Europe?
51431.e: The European anthem is a melody from Ludwig van Beethoven’s 9th Symphony. It is called “Ode to Joy”.
51431.m: The European anthem is Beethoven’s “Ode to Joy”.

51432.q: Which country was the last to join the EU (as of 2026)?
51432.e: Croatia joined in 2013 as the 28th country. No new country has joined since then.

51433.q: How many countries made the start of today’s EU with the EEC in 1957?
51433.e: Belgium, Germany, France, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands founded the European Economic Community in 1957. Later it became the EU.
51433.m: Six countries laid the foundation of the EU in 1957.

51434.q: In which French city does the European Parliament meet?
51434.e: The European Parliament has its official seat in Strasbourg. Most of the big sessions take place there.
51434.m: The EU Parliament meets in Strasbourg.

51435.q: What is the money in many EU countries called?
51435.e: In many EU countries people pay with the euro. That is why this area is also called the eurozone.
51435.m: Many EU countries pay with the euro.

51436.q: Which is the biggest euro coin, meaning the one with the highest value?
51436.e: The coin with the highest value is 2 euros. From 5 euros upwards there are notes.
51436.m: The 2-euro coin is the most valuable euro coin.

51437.q: Which is the smallest euro note?
51437.e: The euro note with the lowest value is the 5-euro note. 1 euro and 2 euros are coins.
51437.m: The smallest euro note is the 5-euro note.

51438.q: What is different from country to country on one side of the euro coins?
51438.e: One side is the same everywhere. On the other side, each country shows its own picture.
51438.m: Each euro country designs one side of the coins itself.

51439.q: In which city is the European Central Bank, which looks after the euro?
51439.e: The European Central Bank (ECB) is in Frankfurt am Main in Germany. It makes sure the euro stays stable.
51439.m: The European Central Bank is in Frankfurt.

51440.q: How many different euro coins are there?
51440.e: There are coins of 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 50 cents and of 1 and 2 euros. That makes 8 coins.
51440.m: There are eight different euro coins.

51441.q: How many stars are on the European flag?
51441.e: There are always 12 stars on the European flag. The number does not change when new countries join.
51441.m: The European flag has twelve stars.

51442.q: How many points does each star on the European flag have?
51442.e: Each star on the flag has five points.
51442.m: The stars on the European flag have five points.

51443.q: What do the 12 stars on the European flag stand for?
51443.e: The 12 stars in a circle are a sign of unity and togetherness. They do not stand for individual countries.
51443.m: The twelve stars are a sign of unity.

51444.q: How many golden stars does the European flag have?
51444.e: The European flag shows 12 golden stars in a circle on a blue background. The number stays the same, however many countries are members.

51445.q: The European flag comes from the Council of Europe. Is Switzerland a member of the Council of Europe?
51445.e: Switzerland has been a member of the Council of Europe since 1963. But it is not in the EU.
51445.m: Switzerland is in the Council of Europe, but not in the EU.

51446.q: Is there anything in the middle of the European flag?
51446.e: The middle of the flag is simply blue. The stars are only around the outside, in a circle.
51446.m: The middle of the European flag is empty and blue.

51447.q: Where do you often see the European flag?
51447.e: The European flag often flies outside EU buildings and next to the flags of the countries.
51447.m: The European flag flies outside many EU buildings.

51448.q: How do you say “thank you” in Italian?
51448.e: “Grazie” is Italian. “Merci” is French and “Gracias” is Spanish.

51449.q: Which language is spoken in Portugal?
51449.e: In Portugal people speak Portuguese. This language is also spoken in Brazil.

51450.q: How do you say “hello” in Spanish?
51450.e: “Hola” means “hello” in Spanish. The H is not pronounced.

51451.q: Which language is spoken in Poland?
51451.e: In Poland people speak Polish. It is related to Czech and Slovak.

51452.q: Which language has its own alphabet with letters such as α and β?
51452.e: Greek has the Greek alphabet. It begins with alpha (α) and beta (β).
51452.m: Greek is written with the Greek alphabet.

51453.q: How many official languages does the EU have (as of 2025)?
51453.e: The EU has 24 official languages. Important texts are translated into all of these languages.

51454.q: How do you say “good day” in French?
51454.e: “Bonjour” is French. “Buongiorno” is Italian, “Buenos días” Spanish and “Goedendag” Dutch.

51455.q: Which language is spoken in Sweden?
51455.e: In Sweden people speak Swedish. It is related to Norwegian and Danish.

51456.q: What is the capital of Great Britain?
51456.e: London is on the Thames and is the capital of Great Britain.
51456.m: London is the capital of Great Britain.

51457.q: What is the capital of Ireland?
51457.e: Dublin is the capital of Ireland. Belfast is in Northern Ireland, which belongs to the United Kingdom.
51457.m: Dublin is the capital of Ireland.

51458.q: What is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina?
51458.e: Sarajevo is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The city lies in a valley surrounded by mountains.
51458.m: Sarajevo is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

51459.q: What is the capital of Slovenia?
51459.e: Ljubljana is the capital of Slovenia. The country borders Italy and Austria.
51459.m: Ljubljana is the capital of Slovenia.

51460.q: What is the capital of Scotland?
51460.e: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland. An old castle stands high above the city.
51460.m: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland.

51461.q: What is the capital of the Netherlands?
51461.e: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands. The city is known for its canals and bikes.
51461.m: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands.

51462.q: Which tiny country lies in the middle of the city of Rome?
51462.e: Vatican City lies entirely within Rome. The Pope lives there.
51462.m: Vatican City lies in the middle of Rome.

51463.q: What do Monaco, Andorra and San Marino have in common?
a: They are all by the sea
They all have the same king
51463.e: Monaco, Andorra and San Marino are very small countries. They are called microstates.
51463.m: Very small countries are called microstates.

51464.q: Is Liechtenstein bigger or smaller than the canton of Zurich?
51464.e: Liechtenstein covers only about 160 square kilometres. The canton of Zurich is more than ten times as big.
51464.m: Liechtenstein is much smaller than the canton of Zurich.

51465.q: Which small country is completely surrounded by Italy and is not in Rome?
51465.e: San Marino lies on a mountain in Italy near the Adriatic. It is surrounded by Italy on all sides.
51465.m: San Marino is completely surrounded by Italy.

51466.q: Which of these microstates is the biggest?
51466.e: Luxembourg covers about 2600 square kilometres. Andorra, Liechtenstein and Monaco are much smaller.
51466.m: Luxembourg is bigger than Andorra, Liechtenstein and Monaco.

51467.q: Which small country is made up of islands in the Mediterranean?
51467.e: Malta is made up of several islands in the Mediterranean, south of Sicily.
51467.m: Malta is an island country in the Mediterranean.

51468.q: Which language is spoken in San Marino?
51468.e: In San Marino Italian is the official language.
51468.m: In San Marino people speak Italian.

51469.q: Which language is the official language in Monaco?
51469.e: In Monaco French is the official language. Some people also still speak the old Monegasque language.

51470.q: Which microstate is the second smallest country in the world?
51470.e: Monaco covers only about 2 square kilometres. Only Vatican City is even smaller.
51470.m: Monaco is the second smallest country in the world.

51471.q: At what time of year are there Christmas markets?
51471.e: Christmas markets are usually held in the weeks before Christmas, that is, during Advent.
51471.m: Christmas markets take place during Advent.

51472.q: Which hot nuts do people often buy in a paper bag at the Christmas market?
51472.e: Marroni are roasted sweet chestnuts. In Switzerland they are sold hot at stalls in winter.

51473.q: Which heart with writing in icing do people often buy at the Christmas market?
51473.e: Gingerbread hearts are decorated with icing and hang on a ribbon. You can give them as presents.
51473.m: There are gingerbread hearts at the Christmas market.

51474.q: What is the warm fruit juice with spices that children drink at the Christmas market called?
51474.e: Children’s punch is a warm fruit juice with spices such as cinnamon. It contains no alcohol.
51474.m: Children drink children’s punch at the Christmas market.

51475.q: In which German city does the Christ Child open the famous Christkindlesmarkt?
51475.e: The Nuremberg Christkindlesmarkt is world-famous. Every year the Christ Child opens it with a prologue.
51475.m: The Christ Child opens the market in Nuremberg.

51476.q: Which city in France calls itself the “Capital of Christmas”?
51476.e: Strasbourg in Alsace has one of the oldest Christmas markets in France. The city calls itself “Capitale de Noël”.
51476.m: Strasbourg calls itself the Capital of Christmas.

51477.q: Where in Zurich is there a big Christmas market under one roof?
51477.e: Every year during Advent there is a big Christmas market in the station hall of Zurich main station. There you are sheltered from rain and snow.
51477.m: In Zurich there is a Christmas market in the main station.

51478.q: The Christmas market in Dresden is called the Striezelmarkt. What is a “Striezel”?
51478.e: The Dresden Striezelmarkt has existed since 1434. “Striezel” is another word for Christmas stollen.
51478.m: A Striezel is a Christmas stollen.

51479.q: On which lake is the “Montreux Noël” Christmas market?
51479.e: Montreux is in the canton of Vaud on Lake Geneva. Every year there is a big Christmas market on the lakeside.
51479.m: Montreux Noël is on Lake Geneva.

51480.q: Which Christmas decoration turns because of the warmth of candles?
51480.e: With a Christmas pyramid, warm air rises from the candles and turns a propeller. It comes from the Ore Mountains.
51480.m: The Christmas pyramid turns with the warmth of candles.

51481.q: Which sweet syrup from Canada do some people like to pour over waffles?
51481.e: Maple syrup is made from the sap of maple trees. Many maple trees grow in Canada.
51481.m: Maple syrup is a sweet syrup from maple trees.

51482.q: Which appliance do you use to make waffles?
51482.e: The batter goes between two hot patterned plates. That is how the waffle is made.
51482.m: Waffles are made in a waffle iron.

51483.q: What pattern does a waffle have?
51483.e: The plates in the waffle iron have a grid. That is why the waffle has lots of little squares.
51483.m: A waffle has a pattern of little squares.

51484.q: Which waffle from Belgium is roundish and has crunchy bits of sugar?
51484.e: The Liège waffle has pearl sugar in the dough. When it is baked, the sugar turns into crunchy caramel.
51484.m: The Liège waffle has pearl sugar in the dough.

51485.q: Which Belgian waffle is rectangular, light and has deep holes?
51485.e: The Brussels waffle is large, rectangular and airy. Lots of topping fits into its deep holes.
51485.m: The Brussels waffle is rectangular and airy.

51486.q: What white powder is often sprinkled on a waffle?
51486.e: Icing sugar is very finely ground sugar. It looks like snow on the waffle.
51486.m: Icing sugar is often sprinkled on waffles.

51487.q: What makes the Belgian Liège waffle special?
a: Coarse lumps of sugar in the dough
It is baked in the oven
51487.e: Pearl sugar goes into the dough of the Liège waffle. When baked it caramelises and makes the waffle sweet and crunchy.
51487.m: The Liège waffle contains pearl sugar.

51488.q: What shape are the waffles from many home waffle irons?
51488.e: Many home waffle irons make a round waffle that is made up of several hearts.

51489.q: Which fruit do people often eat with whipped cream on a waffle?
51489.e: Strawberries and whipped cream are a popular waffle topping. Lemons, grapefruits and raw quinces are too sour for it.
51489.m: Strawberries and whipped cream go well on waffles.

51490.q: What do you need, among other things, for waffle batter?
51490.e: A simple waffle batter is made of flour, eggs, milk, butter and sugar.
51490.m: For waffle batter you need flour, eggs and milk.

51491.q: Which is the largest country in Europe?
51491.e: By area, Russia is the largest country in Europe. It is much bigger than all the other countries on the continent.
51491.m: Russia is the largest country in Europe.

51492.q: Is Russia also the largest country in the whole world?
51492.e: With over 17 million square kilometres, Russia is the largest country on Earth. Canada is the second largest.
51492.m: Russia is the largest country in the world.

51493.q: Which train runs right across Russia from Moscow to the Pacific?
51493.e: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from Moscow to Vladivostok. The route is over 9000 kilometres long and the journey takes about a week.
51493.m: The Trans-Siberian Railway crosses the whole of Russia.

51494.q: What colours is the flag of Russia?
51494.e: The Russian flag has three horizontal stripes: white at the top, blue in the middle and red at the bottom.
51494.m: The flag of Russia is white, blue and red.

51495.q: What are the Russian wooden dolls that fit inside each other called?
51495.e: A matryoshka is a painted wooden doll. When you open it, there is a smaller doll inside, and inside that another one.
51495.m: Matryoshkas are dolls that fit inside each other.

51496.q: Roughly how many times would Switzerland fit into Russia?
51496.e: Russia covers about 17.1 million square kilometres, Switzerland about 41,000. So Russia is more than 400 times as big.
51496.m: Switzerland would fit into Russia over 400 times.

51497.q: Which Russian city is the second largest in the country?
51497.e: St Petersburg is on the Baltic Sea and is the largest city in Russia after Moscow.
51497.m: St Petersburg is the second largest city in Russia.

51498.e: Europe is a part of the world, that is, a continent. Many countries belong to it, including Switzerland.

51499.q: Which half of the Earth is Europe in, if you take the equator as the dividing line?
51499.e: Europe lies entirely north of the equator. That is why it is part of the Northern Hemisphere.
51499.m: Europe is in the Northern Hemisphere.

51500.q: Which ocean lies to the west of Europe?
51500.e: To the west of Europe lies the Atlantic Ocean. On the other side is America.
51500.m: The Atlantic lies to the west of Europe.

51501.q: Which continent lies south of Europe, on the other side of the Mediterranean?
51501.e: Africa begins south of the Mediterranean. Between Spain and Morocco the sea is only narrow.

51502.q: Which continent is Europe joined to by land?
51502.e: Europe and Asia together form one big landmass. It is called Eurasia.
51502.m: Europe and Asia together form Eurasia.

51503.q: Is Europe a rather small or a rather big continent?
51503.e: Europe is the second smallest continent. Only Australia is smaller.
51503.m: Europe is the second smallest continent.

51504.q: Which ocean lies in the far north of Europe?
51504.e: In the far north of Europe the cold Arctic Ocean begins. It is often full of ice there.
51504.m: The Arctic Ocean lies to the north of Europe.

51505.e: Switzerland is in central Europe, in the Alps. It has no sea.
51505.m: Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe.

a: A king’s daughter from a Greek legend
51506.e: In a Greek legend, the god Zeus carries off the king’s daughter Europa. The continent is named after her.
51506.m: Europe gets its name from a figure in a Greek legend.

51507.q: How many continents are there according to the usual count at school?
51507.e: Usually seven continents are counted: Europe, Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Australia and Antarctica.

51508.q: On which lake is the city of Geneva?
51508.e: Geneva lies at the south-western end of Lake Geneva. There the water flows out of the lake and on into France.
51508.m: Geneva lies at the end of Lake Geneva.

51509.q: Which river flows out of Lake Geneva at Geneva?
51509.e: The Rhône comes from Valais, flows through Lake Geneva and leaves it at Geneva. Then it flows on into France.
51509.m: In Geneva the Rhône leaves Lake Geneva.

51510.q: Which neighbouring country borders the canton of Geneva almost everywhere?
51510.e: The canton of Geneva is almost completely surrounded by France. Only a small part borders the canton of Vaud.
51510.m: The canton of Geneva is almost completely surrounded by France.

51511.q: Which aid organisation was founded in Geneva in 1863?
51511.e: Henry Dunant from Geneva founded the Red Cross together with others. It helps the wounded and people in need.
51511.m: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva.

51512.q: Which festival does Geneva celebrate every year in December?
51512.e: The Escalade recalls the year 1602, when Geneva fought off an attack. A soup pot made of chocolate is smashed as part of it.
51512.m: At the Escalade, the people of Geneva smash a chocolate pot.

51513.q: What is made of flowers in the English Garden in Geneva?
51513.e: The Flower Clock in the English Garden tells the time. Its face is made of thousands of flowers.
51513.m: Geneva has a clock made of flowers.

51514.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of Geneva?
51514.e: The Geneva coat of arms shows half an eagle on the left and a key on the right. Both stand for the city’s old history.
51514.m: The Geneva coat of arms has half an eagle and a key.

51515.q: In which city is the Jet d’Eau?
51515.e: The Jet d’Eau is a huge fountain in Lake Geneva. It is the best-known landmark of Geneva.
51515.m: The Jet d’Eau is the landmark of Geneva.

51516.e: The Jet d’Eau shoots water high into the air. “Jet d’eau” means “water jet” in English.
51516.m: The Jet d’Eau is a huge fountain.

51517.q: About how high does the Jet d’Eau shoot?
51517.e: The jet of water reaches about 140 metres. That is higher than a 40-storey tower block.
51517.m: The Jet d’Eau shoots about 140 metres high.

51518.q: Where does the water for the Jet d’Eau come from?
51518.e: Pumps take the water straight from Lake Geneva. Afterwards it falls back into the lake.
51518.m: The Jet d’Eau takes its water from Lake Geneva.

51519.q: Where exactly is the Jet d’Eau?
51519.e: The fountain stands in the lake by the shore of Geneva. A jetty leads close to it.
51519.m: The Jet d’Eau stands right in Lake Geneva.

51520.q: What can you often see in the spray of the Jet d’Eau when the sun is shining?
51520.e: The sun shines through the fine water droplets. This often creates the bright colours of a rainbow.
51520.m: You can often see a rainbow in the Jet d’Eau.

51521.q: Why was the Jet d’Eau first built in 1886?
a: As a valve for water pressure
51521.e: At first, a waterworks released excess water pressure through a jet. Because people found it beautiful, it was later turned into a proper fountain.
51521.m: The Jet d’Eau was first a valve for excess water pressure.

51522.q: When is the Jet d’Eau sometimes switched off?
51522.e: In strong wind the water would be blown onto roads and people. It is also switched off when there is frost.
51522.m: The Jet d’Eau is switched off in strong wind.

51523.q: How fast does the water shoot out of the nozzle of the Jet d’Eau?
51523.e: The water leaves the nozzle at about 200 kilometres per hour. That is as fast as a fast train.
51523.m: The water of the Jet d’Eau travels at about 200 km/h.

51524.q: What is the capital of the canton of Vaud called?
51524.e: Lausanne is the capital of the canton of Vaud. The city lies on Lake Geneva.
51524.m: Lausanne is the capital of Vaud.

51525.q: What colours is the flag of the canton of Vaud?
51525.e: The Vaud flag is white at the top and green at the bottom. In the white part there is a motto in gold letters.
51525.m: The Vaud flag is white and green.

51526.q: Which words are on the flag of Vaud?
51526.e: “Liberté et Patrie” means “Freedom and Fatherland”. These words are written in gold letters on the flag.
51526.m: The Vaud flag says “Liberté et Patrie”.

51527.q: Which famous castle in the canton of Vaud stands right on Lake Geneva?
51527.e: Chillon Castle stands on a rock in Lake Geneva near Montreux. It is one of the most visited castles in Switzerland.
51527.m: Chillon Castle stands on a rock in Lake Geneva.

51528.q: Since which year has Vaud been a canton of Switzerland?
51528.e: Before that, Vaud belonged to Bern for a long time. In 1803 it became a canton of its own.
51528.m: Vaud has been a Swiss canton since 1803.

51529.q: Which two large lakes does the canton of Vaud have a share of?
51529.e: Lake Geneva lies to the south, Lake Neuchâtel to the north. Both belong partly to Vaud.
51529.m: Vaud lies on Lake Geneva and Lake Neuchâtel.

51530.q: Which town in the canton of Vaud lies at the southern end of Lake Neuchâtel?
51530.e: Yverdon-les-Bains lies where Lake Neuchâtel ends in the south. The town is known for its warm healing waters.
51530.m: Yverdon-les-Bains lies at the southern end of Lake Neuchâtel.

51531.q: Which dish from Vaud is made of leeks, potatoes and sausage?
51531.e: Papet vaudois is a mash of leeks and potatoes. It is eaten with a Vaud sausage.
51531.m: Papet vaudois is a leek dish from Vaud.

51532.q: Which sports organisation has its headquarters in Lausanne?
51532.e: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) is based in Lausanne. It organises the Olympic Games.
51532.m: The Olympic Committee has its headquarters in Lausanne.

51533.q: Which nickname does Lausanne have because of sport?
51533.e: Lausanne calls itself the “Olympic Capital”. Many large sports federations have their headquarters there.
51533.m: Lausanne is also called the “Olympic Capital”.

51534.q: Which museum in Lausanne shows torches and medals from the Games?
51534.e: The Olympic Museum stands in Ouchy on the lakeshore. It shows torches, medals and stories of the Olympic Games.
51534.m: In the Olympic Museum in Lausanne you can see Olympic torches.

51535.q: What does the watchman of Lausanne Cathedral call out from the tower every hour at night?
51535.e: From 10 pm to 2 am a watchman calls out every full hour from the tower. This old tradition has existed for centuries.
51535.m: In Lausanne a tower watchman calls out the hours at night.

51536.q: Which means of transport travels uphill under the city in Lausanne?
51536.e: Lausanne has a metro. Line M2 climbs very steeply up from the lake.

51537.q: What is the district of Lausanne right on the lakeshore called?
51537.e: Ouchy lies down by Lake Geneva and has a harbour. Boats leave from there for France and other places.

51538.q: Which high court of Switzerland has its seat in Lausanne?
a: The European Court of Human Rights
51538.e: The Federal Supreme Court is the highest court in Switzerland. Its main seat is in Lausanne. The Federal Criminal Court is in Bellinzona.
51538.m: The Federal Supreme Court is in Lausanne.

51539.q: What is the landscape of the city of Lausanne like?
a: In a valley with no lake
51539.e: Lausanne lies on a steep slope above Lake Geneva. Many streets and stairs go steeply uphill.
51539.m: Lausanne is a very hilly city.

51540.q: Which large university stands in Lausanne?
51540.e: EPFL is the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne. It is one of the two federal technical universities.
51540.m: EPFL, the federal institute of technology, is in Lausanne.

51541.q: Which lake is the largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland?
51541.e: Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are larger, but they also lie in other countries. Lake Neuchâtel lies entirely in Switzerland.
51541.m: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland.

51542.q: What is the canton of Neuchâtel especially known for?
51542.e: Watches have been made in the Neuchâtel Jura for a long time. Many well-known watch companies have their workshops there.
51542.m: Neuchâtel is known for its watches.

51543.q: Which watchmaking town in the canton of Neuchâtel is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
51543.e: La Chaux-de-Fonds became World Heritage together with Le Locle in 2009. Its streets were planned for the watchmakers.
51543.m: La Chaux-de-Fonds is a World Heritage watchmaking town.

51544.q: What is the Creux du Van in the canton of Neuchâtel?
51544.e: The Creux du Van is a huge, round basin of rock walls. Ibex and chamois live there.
51544.m: The Creux du Van is a large rock basin.

51545.q: In which mountain range is the northern part of the canton of Neuchâtel?
51545.e: The canton of Neuchâtel lies between Lake Neuchâtel and the Jura. The watchmaking towns lie high up in the Jura.
51545.m: A large part of Neuchâtel lies in the Jura.

51546.q: What colours is the flag of the canton of Neuchâtel?
51546.e: The Neuchâtel flag has three vertical stripes in green, white and red. At the top of the red part there is a white cross.
51546.m: The Neuchâtel flag is green, white and red.

51547.q: Which kingdom did Neuchâtel once belong to?
51547.e: Neuchâtel belonged to the King of Prussia for a long time. At the same time it had been a Swiss canton since 1815.
51547.m: Neuchâtel once belonged to the King of Prussia.

51548.q: Which two languages are spoken in the canton of Fribourg?
51548.e: The canton of Fribourg is bilingual. Most people speak French, many others German.
51548.m: In the canton of Fribourg people speak French and German.

51549.q: What is the French name of the town called Freiburg in German?
51549.e: In French, Freiburg is called Fribourg. In the town many street signs are in both languages.
51549.m: In French, Freiburg is called Fribourg.

51550.q: Which river in Fribourg often separates German and French?
51550.e: The river is called Sarine in French and Saane in German. West of it people mostly speak French, east of it mostly German.
51550.m: The Sarine often separates German and French.

51551.q: Which famous cheese comes from the canton of Fribourg?
51551.e: Gruyère is a hard cheese made from cow’s milk. It ripens for many months in the cheese cellar.
51551.m: Gruyère cheese comes from the canton of Fribourg.

51552.q: What colours is the flag of the canton of Fribourg?
51552.e: The Fribourg flag is black at the top and white at the bottom. So it has only two colours.
51552.m: The Fribourg flag is black and white.

51553.q: Which fondue made from two kinds of cheese is typical of Fribourg?
51553.e: “Moitié-moitié” means “half and half”. Gruyère and Vacherin Fribourgeois are mixed.
51553.m: Fondue moitié-moitié is half Gruyère and half Vacherin.

51554.q: Which little town in the canton of Fribourg has a castle on a hill and gave its name to a cheese?
51554.e: Gruyères is a small town with a castle. In German it is called Greyerz.
51554.m: Gruyères is a little town with a castle in the canton of Fribourg.

51555.q: Which bilingual town on a lake belongs to the canton of Fribourg?
51555.e: Murten lies on Lake Murten and has an old town wall. Most people there speak German.
51555.m: Murten on Lake Murten belongs to the canton of Fribourg.

51556.q: Which chocolate brand has its factory in Broc in the canton of Fribourg?
51556.e: Cailler has made chocolate in Broc since 1898. You can visit the factory and taste chocolate.
51556.m: Cailler chocolate comes from Broc in the canton of Fribourg.

51557.q: In which year was the canton of Jura founded?
51557.e: The canton of Jura was created on 1 January 1979. Before that, the area was part of another canton.
51557.m: The canton of Jura has existed since 1979.

51558.q: Which canton did the Jura belong to in the past?
51558.e: The area of today’s canton of Jura belonged to Bern for a long time. Many people from the Jura wanted a canton of their own.
51558.m: The Jura used to belong to the canton of Bern.

51559.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Jura?
51559.e: In the canton of Jura, French is spoken almost everywhere. Only in one village, Ederswiler, do people speak German.
51559.m: In the canton of Jura people speak French.

51560.q: What can be seen on the flag of the canton of Jura?
51560.e: The flag shows a red bishop’s staff and red and white stripes. The staff recalls the bishops of Basel, who once ruled there.
51560.m: The Jura flag has a bishop’s staff on it.

51561.q: What is the hilly plateau with pastures and horses in the canton of Jura called?
51561.e: The Franches-Montagnes are called Freiberge in German. Many horses graze freely in the meadows there.
51561.m: The Franches-Montagnes are a plateau in the Jura.

51562.q: What is the pretty little town on the river Doubs in the canton of Jura called?
51562.e: Saint-Ursanne lies on the Doubs and has an old stone bridge. The little town is very well preserved.
51562.m: Saint-Ursanne lies on the Doubs in the Jura.

51563.q: What grows on the terraces in Lavaux?
51563.e: Lavaux is a large wine-growing area. The vines grow on steep terraces.
51563.m: In Lavaux, grapevines grow on terraces.

51564.q: On which lake are the vineyards of Lavaux?
51564.e: The vineyards climb up from the shore of Lake Geneva. From there you have a wide view over the lake.

51565.e: Lavaux lies in the canton of Vaud. It stretches from Lausanne to near Montreux.
51565.m: Lavaux lies in the canton of Vaud.

51566.q: Since which year has Lavaux been a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
51566.e: In 2007 UNESCO added the vineyard terraces of Lavaux to the World Heritage List. This is meant to protect them for ever.
51566.m: Lavaux has been World Heritage since 2007.

51567.q: What are the walls of the vineyard terraces in Lavaux made of?
51567.e: Stone walls hold the soil in place on the steep slopes. They also store the warmth of the sun.
51567.m: The vineyard terraces in Lavaux have stone walls.

51568.q: Which wine is mainly produced in Lavaux?
51568.e: The white Chasselas grape is the main grape in Lavaux. White wine is made from it.

51569.q: Who laid out the vineyard terraces in Lavaux many hundreds of years ago?
51569.e: In the Middle Ages, monks from monasteries laid out the terraces. You can still see their work today.
51569.m: Monks laid out the terraces in Lavaux.

51570.q: Which “three suns” do people talk about in Lavaux?
51570.e: The vines get sun from the sky, the light is reflected by the lake and the walls give off warmth. That is why it is so good for vines there.
51570.m: In Lavaux the sky, the lake and the walls warm the vines.

51571.q: In which season are the grapes harvested in Lavaux?
51571.e: The grapes are ripe in autumn. Then many helpers pick the grapes on the steep slopes.
51571.m: In Lavaux the grapes are harvested in autumn.

51572.e: Romandy is the part of Switzerland where French is spoken. It lies in the west of the country.

51573.q: In which part of Switzerland is Romandy?
51573.e: Romandy lies in the west of Switzerland on the border with France. It is also called Western Switzerland.
51573.m: Romandy lies in the west of Switzerland.

51574.q: What are the people from Romandy called?
51574.e: The people from French-speaking Switzerland are called Romands. The word comes from French.
51574.m: The people of Romandy are called Romands.

51575.q: What is the imaginary border between German-speaking Switzerland and Romandy called?
51575.e: The Röstigraben, or “rösti ditch”, is not a real border but a joke name. It separates German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland.
51575.m: The Röstigraben separates German and French in Switzerland.

51576.q: Which city is the largest city in Romandy?
51576.e: Geneva is the largest city in Romandy. About 200,000 people live there.
51576.m: Geneva is the largest city in Romandy.

51577.q: Which of these cantons is entirely French-speaking?
51577.e: Geneva, Vaud, Neuchâtel and Jura are French-speaking. Bern, Valais and Fribourg have two languages.
51577.m: Neuchâtel is an entirely French-speaking canton.

51578.q: What else do German-speaking Swiss call Romandy?
51578.e: Many German-speaking Swiss call Romandy “Welschland”. The people there are called Welsche.
51578.m: In Swiss German, Romandy is also called Welschland.

51579.q: Which bilingual canton belongs partly to Romandy?
51579.e: In Lower Valais people speak French, in Upper Valais German. That is why part of Valais belongs to Romandy.
51579.m: The lower part of Valais belongs to Romandy.

51580.q: Which lake lies in the middle of Romandy, between Switzerland and France?
51580.e: Lake Geneva is the largest lake in Romandy. Its southern shore belongs to France.

51581.q: What is the number 70 called in Romandy?
51581.e: In France people say soixante-dix. In Switzerland they say the simpler septante.

51582.q: What is the number 90 called in Romandy?
51582.e: In France people say quatre-vingt-dix. In Switzerland and Belgium they say nonante.

51583.q: What is the number 80 called in Vaud?
51583.e: In Vaud, Valais and Fribourg many people say huitante. In France people say quatre-vingts.

51584.q: What is Lake Geneva usually called in French?
51584.e: In French, Lake Geneva is called Lac Léman. Sometimes people also say Lac de Genève.
51584.m: In French, Lake Geneva is called Lac Léman.

51585.q: What do many Romands call lunch?
51585.e: In Switzerland, dîner is lunch. In France lunch is usually called déjeuner.
51585.m: In Romandy lunch is called dîner.

51586.q: What do many Romands call the evening meal?
51586.e: In Romandy people eat souper in the evening. This word is hardly used in France any more.
51586.m: In Romandy the evening meal is called souper.

51587.q: By number of speakers, where does French rank among Switzerland’s national languages?
51587.e: Most people speak German, followed by French. A good one in five people in Switzerland speaks French.
51587.m: French is the second largest national language.

51588.q: Which famous music festival takes place in Montreux every summer?
51588.e: The Montreux Jazz Festival takes place every year in July. Musicians from all over the world play there.
51588.m: The Jazz Festival takes place in Montreux.

51589.q: Since which year has the Montreux Jazz Festival existed?
51589.e: Claude Nobs founded the festival in 1967. Today musicians come from all over the world.
51589.m: The Montreux Jazz Festival has existed since 1967.

51590.q: Which singer has a statue on the lakeshore in Montreux?
51590.e: Freddie Mercury of the band Queen often worked in Montreux. The statue has stood by the lake since 1996.
51590.m: There is a statue of Freddie Mercury in Montreux.

51591.q: Which old boats sail across Lake Geneva from Montreux?
51591.e: The shipping company CGN has several old paddle steamers with large paddle wheels. They also stop in Montreux.
51591.m: Old paddle steamers sail across the lake from Montreux.

51592.q: Which plants grow on the lakeshore in Montreux because of the mild climate?
51592.e: Montreux is protected from cold wind by mountains. That is why even palm trees grow on the shore.
51592.m: Palm trees grow by the lake in Montreux.

51593.q: Which animals can you see in a park at the top of the Rochers de Naye near Montreux?
51593.e: On the Rochers de Naye there is a park with marmots. From up there you can see far across Lake Geneva.
51593.m: Marmots live on the Rochers de Naye.

51594.q: Which kind of railway takes you from Montreux up the Rochers de Naye?
51594.e: The cog railway runs from Montreux almost to the summit. From up there you have a lovely view of Lake Geneva.
51594.m: A cog railway runs from Montreux up the Rochers de Naye.

51595.q: Which panoramic train connects Montreux with the Bernese Oberland?
51595.e: The GoldenPass line runs from Montreux via Zweisimmen towards Interlaken. It passes through mountains and valleys.
51595.m: The GoldenPass connects Montreux with the Bernese Oberland.

51596.q: Which area on Lake Geneva with Montreux and Vevey is also called a riviera?
51596.e: The area around Vevey and Montreux is called the Vaud Riviera. It is known for its mild climate.
51596.m: Montreux lies on the Vaud Riviera.

51597.q: When is a large Christmas market held by the lake in Montreux?
51597.e: The “Montreux Noël” Christmas market stands on the lakeshore. It begins at the end of November and lasts into December.
51597.m: Montreux has a Christmas market in December.

51598.q: What is the large concert hall right on the lake in Lucerne called?
51598.e: The KKL Luzern is a culture and convention centre on the shore of Lake Lucerne. Many concerts take place there.
51598.m: The KKL is the big concert hall in Lucerne.

51599.q: Where in Lucerne can you see large holes in the rock from the Ice Age?
51599.e: In the Glacier Garden in Lucerne you can see glacial potholes. Meltwater from the glaciers drilled them into the rock long ago.
51599.m: In the Glacier Garden in Lucerne you can see traces of the Ice Age.

51600.q: Which loud festival with brass bands does Lucerne celebrate every year?
51600.e: Lucerne Carnival is one of the largest carnivals in Switzerland. Many Guggenmusik bands then parade through the old town.
51600.m: Lucerne celebrates a big carnival every year.

51601.q: What happened to the Chapel Bridge in 1993?
51601.e: On the night of 18 August 1993, a large part of the Chapel Bridge burned. It was quickly rebuilt.

51602.q: What hangs up under the roof of the Chapel Bridge?
51602.e: Triangular painted picture panels hang under the roof. They show scenes from the history of Lucerne.
51602.m: Painted pictures hang under the roof of the Chapel Bridge.

51603.q: In which century was the Chapel Bridge built?
51603.e: The Chapel Bridge was built in the 14th century, in the Middle Ages. It is one of the oldest wooden bridges in Europe.
51603.m: The Chapel Bridge dates from the Middle Ages.

51604.q: Who is allowed to cross the Chapel Bridge today?
51604.e: The Chapel Bridge is a bridge for pedestrians only. Cars use other bridges.
51604.m: You cross the Chapel Bridge on foot.

51605.q: Which church is the Chapel Bridge named after?
51605.e: The bridge begins near St Peter’s Chapel. That is why it is called the Chapel Bridge.
51605.m: The Chapel Bridge takes its name from St Peter’s Chapel.

51606.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of the canton of Uri?
51606.e: The Uri coat of arms shows a black bull’s head on a yellow background. It is called the Uri bull.
51606.m: The coat of arms of Uri has a bull’s head.

51607.q: Which famous Alpine pass is in the canton of Uri?
51607.e: The Gotthard Pass leads from Uri to Ticino. It is one of the most important routes across the Alps.
51607.m: The Gotthard Pass is in the canton of Uri.

51608.q: Which very long railway tunnel begins in the north in the canton of Uri?
51608.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel begins at Erstfeld in Uri. At about 57 kilometres, it is the longest railway tunnel in the world (as of 2025).
51608.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel begins in the canton of Uri.

51609.q: Which mountain village in Uri is a well-known winter sports resort?
51609.e: Andermatt lies in the Urseren valley in the canton of Uri. You can go skiing there in winter.
51609.m: Andermatt is a winter sports resort in the canton of Uri.

51610.q: Which old cantons does Uri belong to, together with Schwyz and Unterwalden?
51610.e: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are called the founding cantons. They are seen as the beginning of the Swiss Confederation.
51610.m: Uri is one of the three founding cantons.

51611.q: According to legend, which village in Uri did William Tell come from?
51611.e: According to legend, William Tell lived in Bürglen near Altdorf. Today there is a Tell Museum there.
51611.m: According to legend, William Tell came from Bürglen in Uri.

51612.q: Which country gets its name from the canton of Schwyz?
51612.e: Already in the Middle Ages, all the Confederates were called “Schwyzer”. This became the German name “Schweiz”, Switzerland.
51612.m: Switzerland gets its name from the canton of Schwyz.

51613.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Schwyz look like?
a: Red with a small white cross
51613.e: The Schwyz coat of arms is red with a small white cross in the top corner. It recalls the Swiss flag.
51613.m: The coat of arms of Schwyz is red with a small white cross.

51614.q: Which large monastery stands in the canton of Schwyz?
51614.e: Einsiedeln Abbey is a Benedictine monastery. Many people go there on pilgrimage.
51614.m: Einsiedeln Abbey is in the canton of Schwyz.

51615.q: What are the two pointed mountains above the town of Schwyz called?
51615.e: The Grosser and Kleiner Mythen rise above Schwyz. They are a landmark of the canton.
51615.m: The Mythen are Schwyz’s local mountains.

51616.q: Which huge cave lies in the Muota valley?
51616.e: The Hölloch in the Muota valley is one of the longest caves in the world. Explorers keep discovering new passages there.
51616.m: The Hölloch is in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz.

51617.q: In which town can you see the old Federal Charter of the Confederates today?
51617.e: The Federal Charter is kept in the Museum of the Swiss Charters of Confederation in Schwyz. It is an important document from the early history of the Swiss Confederation.
51617.m: The Federal Charter is kept in the museum in Schwyz.

51618.q: On which lake is the Schwyz village of Brunnen?
51618.e: Brunnen lies on the shore of Lake Lucerne. Boats cross the lake from there.

51619.q: What is the capital of the canton of Obwalden called?
51619.e: Sarnen is the capital of Obwalden. The town lies on Lake Sarnen.
51619.m: Sarnen is the capital of Obwalden.

51620.q: Which mountain resort belongs to Obwalden but is completely separate from the rest of the canton?
51620.e: Engelberg has belonged to Obwalden since 1815. Nidwalden lies between Engelberg and the rest of the canton.
51620.m: Engelberg belongs to Obwalden but is separate from the rest of the canton.

51621.q: Which glacier mountain is the highest mountain in Obwalden?
51621.e: Titlis is about 3238 metres high. You go up by cable car from Engelberg.
51621.m: Titlis is the highest mountain in Obwalden.

51622.q: Which hermit from Obwalden is the patron saint of Switzerland?
51622.e: Brother Klaus’s real name was Niklaus von Flüe. He lived as a hermit in the Ranft near Flüeli in Obwalden.
51622.m: Brother Klaus is the patron saint of Switzerland.

51623.q: Which pass leads from Obwalden to the Bernese Oberland?
51623.e: Over the Brünig Pass you get from Obwalden to Meiringen in the Bernese Oberland. A railway also runs over it.
51623.m: The Brünig Pass connects Obwalden with the Bernese Oberland.

51624.q: Which two colours does the coat of arms of Obwalden have?
51624.e: The coat of arms of Obwalden is red at the top and white at the bottom. On it is a key in the opposite colours.
51624.m: The coat of arms of Obwalden is red and white.

51625.q: With which canton did Obwalden once form Unterwalden?
51625.e: Together, Obwalden and Nidwalden form the old Unterwalden. Today they are two separate cantons.
51625.m: Obwalden and Nidwalden together formed Unterwalden.

51626.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Nidwalden show?
51626.e: The Nidwalden coat of arms is red with a white double key. The key is the symbol of the apostle Peter.
51626.m: The coat of arms of Nidwalden has a key.

51627.q: Up which mountain near Stans does a cable car with an open upper deck run?
51627.e: The “CabriO” cable car runs up the Stanserhorn. You can stand on the open deck on top.
51627.m: A cable car with an open deck runs up the Stanserhorn.

51628.q: Which mountain with large hotels lies high above the lake in Nidwalden?
51628.e: The Bürgenstock is a well-known place for day trips in Nidwalden. From the top you can see far across Lake Lucerne.

51629.q: Which hero has a monument on the village square in Stans?
51629.e: The Winkelried Monument stands on the village square in Stans. According to legend, Winkelried came from Nidwalden.
51629.m: The Winkelried Monument stands in Stans.

51630.q: Which lake does Nidwalden border to the north?
51630.e: Lake Lucerne forms the northern border of Nidwalden. Villages such as Buochs and Beckenried lie on its shore.

51632.q: Which river flows from the Engelberg valley through Nidwalden into the lake?
51632.e: The Engelberger Aa comes from the valley of Engelberg. It flows into Lake Lucerne near Buochs.
51632.m: The Engelberger Aa flows through Nidwalden.

51633.q: Which sweet cake is a speciality from Zug?
51633.e: Zug cherry cake is soaked in kirsch, a cherry brandy. Many cherries have been grown in Zug for a long time.
51633.m: Zug cherry cake is a speciality from Zug.

51634.q: What colours is the coat of arms of the canton of Zug?
51634.e: The Zug coat of arms is white with a blue horizontal band in the middle.
51634.m: The coat of arms of Zug is white and blue.

51635.q: How big is the canton of Zug compared with the other cantons?
a: It is one of the smallest
It is larger than the Grisons
51635.e: The canton of Zug covers only about 239 square kilometres. It is the smallest canton with two seats in the Council of States.
51635.m: The canton of Zug is one of the smallest cantons.

51636.q: Apart from Lake Zug, which lake is also in the canton of Zug?
51636.e: Lake Ägeri lies in the east of the canton of Zug. The Lorze flows out of it towards Lake Zug.
51636.m: Lake Ägeri is in the canton of Zug.

51637.q: Which caves with stalactites can you visit near Baar in the canton of Zug?
51637.e: The Höllgrotten lie near Baar in the Lorze gorge. You can see many stalactites there.
51637.m: The Höllgrotten are near Baar in the canton of Zug.

51638.q: What is the place by Lake Ägeri where a famous battle took place in 1315 called?
51638.e: On 15 November 1315 the Confederates fought a Habsburg army at Morgarten. A monument by Lake Ägeri recalls it.
51638.m: A battle took place at Morgarten by Lake Ägeri in 1315.

51639.q: Which tower with a clock is a landmark of Zug’s old town?
51639.e: The Zytturm is an old clock tower in Zug’s old town. Its roof is blue and white like the Zug coat of arms.
51639.m: The Zytturm is a landmark of Zug.

51640.q: Pilatus is the local mountain of which city?
51640.e: Pilatus stands south-west of Lucerne. You can see it from the whole city.

51641.e: The highest summit of Pilatus is 2128 metres high. That is about 2100 metres.

51642.q: What is special about the Pilatus Railway?
a: It is the steepest cog railway in the world
It is the longest cable car in the world
It is the fastest train in the world
51642.e: At its steepest point, the Pilatus Railway has a gradient of 48 per cent. This makes it the steepest cog railway in the world.
51642.m: The Pilatus Railway is the steepest cog railway in the world.

51643.q: According to old legends, which mythical creature is said to live on Pilatus?
51643.e: In the past people told stories that dragons lived on Pilatus. That is why the dragon is a symbol of the mountain.
51643.m: According to legend, dragons lived on Pilatus.

51644.q: Where does the cog railway up Pilatus start?
51644.e: The Pilatus Railway goes up from Alpnachstad on Lake Alpnach. From there it climbs to Pilatus Kulm.
51644.m: The Pilatus Railway starts in Alpnachstad.

51645.q: In which year was the Pilatus Railway opened?
51645.e: The Pilatus Railway has been running since 1889. So it is more than 130 years old.
51645.m: The Pilatus Railway has run since 1889.

51646.q: Which large lake can you see far below from Pilatus?
51646.e: Pilatus stands right by Lake Lucerne. From the top you can see the lake and the city of Lucerne.
51646.m: From Pilatus you look down on Lake Lucerne.

51647.q: How do you get up Pilatus from Kriens?
51647.e: From Kriens, first a gondola and then an aerial cableway take you up Pilatus. The cog railway runs on the other side, from Alpnachstad.
51647.m: From Kriens you go up Pilatus by cable car.

51648.q: When does the cog railway up Pilatus not run?
51648.e: The Pilatus Railway runs only from about spring to autumn. In winter there is too much snow on the line.
51648.m: The Pilatus Railway does not run in winter.

51649.q: Which lovely nickname does the Rigi have?
51649.e: The Rigi is often called the “Queen of the Mountains”. People once believed its name came from the Latin word for queen.
51649.m: The Rigi is also called the “Queen of the Mountains”.

51650.q: Since which year has a cog railway run up the Rigi?
51650.e: The Vitznau-Rigi Railway has run since 1871. It was the first mountain railway in Europe.
51650.m: A railway has run up the Rigi since 1871.

51651.q: From which village on Lake Lucerne does the oldest Rigi railway go up?
51651.e: The Vitznau-Rigi Railway starts in Vitznau on the lakeshore. From there it runs up to Rigi Kulm.
51651.m: The oldest Rigi railway starts in Vitznau.

51652.q: What is the highest point of the Rigi called?
51652.e: Rigi Kulm is the summit of the Rigi. From there you have a wide view over lakes and mountains.
51652.m: Rigi Kulm is the highest point of the Rigi.

51653.q: About how high is Rigi Kulm?
51653.e: Rigi Kulm is just under 1800 metres high. From there you can see far across lakes and mountains.
51653.m: Rigi Kulm is about 1800 metres high.

51654.q: Which two cantons does the Rigi belong to?
51654.e: Part of the Rigi belongs to the canton of Lucerne, another part to the canton of Schwyz. The summit is in the canton of Schwyz.
51654.m: The Rigi belongs to Lucerne and Schwyz.

51655.q: Which three lakes lie around the Rigi?
a: Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and Lake Lauerz
Lake Geneva, Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Biel
Lake Thun, Lake Brienz and Lake Sarnen
Lake Zurich, Lake Walen and Lake Greifen
51655.e: The Rigi is almost completely surrounded by lakes. Lake Lucerne lies to the south, Lake Zug to the north and Lake Lauerz to the east.
51655.m: The Rigi is surrounded by three lakes.

51656.q: From which place does the second cog railway run up the Rigi?
51656.e: The Arth-Rigi Railway has run up the Rigi from Arth-Goldau since 1875. So you can go up by train from two sides.
51656.m: A railway also runs up the Rigi from Arth-Goldau.

51657.q: Where does Lake Lucerne’s German name “Vierwaldstättersee” come from?
a: From four old cantons on its shores
From four forests in the water
From four islands in the lake
51657.e: The four “Waldstätten” (forest cantons) were Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne. In the past the lake was called the Lake of Lucerne.
51657.m: Lake Lucerne’s German name comes from four old cantons.

51658.q: What is the part of Lake Lucerne that lies in the canton of Uri called?
51658.e: Lake Uri is the south-eastern arm of the lake. It reaches from Brunnen to the mouth of the Reuss near Flüelen and Seedorf.
51658.m: Lake Uri is part of Lake Lucerne.

51659.q: How many cantons border Lake Lucerne today?
51659.e: Today Uri, Schwyz, Nidwalden, Obwalden and Lucerne border the lake. This is because Unterwalden is divided into two cantons.

51660.q: About how deep is Lake Lucerne at its deepest point?
51660.e: The deepest point is 214 metres deep. It lies between Beckenried and Gersau.
51660.m: Lake Lucerne is over 200 metres deep.

51661.q: What is the rock in the lake that honours the author of “William Tell” called?
51661.e: The Schiller Stone is a tall rock in Lake Uri. Its inscription honours Friedrich Schiller, who wrote the play “William Tell”.
51661.m: The Schiller Stone honours Friedrich Schiller.

51662.q: What shape does Lake Lucerne have when seen from above?
a: It is round like a circle
It is straight like a line
It is shaped like a heart
51662.e: The lake has many arms and bays. Near Lucerne, four arms almost form a cross.

51663.q: At which city does Lake Lucerne end in the west?
51663.e: The city of Lucerne lies at the western end of the lake. The water flows out of the lake there.
51663.m: Lucerne lies at the western end of Lake Lucerne.

51664.q: What were the new islands in Lake Uri built from?
51664.e: Small islands were piled up in Lake Uri near Flüelen. They were built from rock dug out during the construction of the Gotthard Base Tunnel.
51664.m: The islands in Lake Uri are made of tunnel rock.

51665.q: Which river from the Muota valley flows into the lake at Brunnen?
51665.e: The Muota flows through the Muota valley. At Brunnen it flows into Lake Lucerne.
51665.m: The Muota flows into Lake Lucerne at Brunnen.

51666.q: According to legend, what did men from the founding cantons do on the Rütli?
51666.e: According to legend, men from Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swore on the Rütli to help one another. This is called the Rütli Oath.
51666.m: The Rütli Oath is said to have taken place on the Rütli.

51667.q: What is the easiest way to get to the Rütli?
51667.e: It is best to go by boat, for example from Brunnen. You can also walk down from Seelisberg.
51667.m: The best way to the Rütli is by boat.

51668.q: On which day is there a big celebration on the Rütli every year?
51668.e: Every year on 1 August there is a celebration on the Rütli. 1 August is the Swiss National Day.
51668.m: On 1 August the National Day is celebrated on the Rütli.

51669.q: Which general gathered his officers on the Rütli meadow in 1940?
51669.e: On 25 July 1940, General Henri Guisan spoke to his officers on the Rütli. He explained to them how Switzerland was to be defended.
51669.m: General Guisan held the Rütli Report in 1940.

51670.q: Which legendary hero has a monument in Altdorf?
51670.e: The Tell Monument stands on the town hall square in Altdorf. It was put up in 1895.
51670.m: The monument to William Tell stands in Altdorf.

51671.q: Who stands next to Tell on the Tell Monument in Altdorf?
51671.e: The monument shows Tell together with his son Walter. The son is holding on to his father.
51671.m: The Tell Monument shows Tell with his son.

51672.q: According to the legend, what did Tell have to shoot off his son's head in Altdorf?
51672.e: The bailiff Gessler forced Tell to shoot an apple off his son's head. Tell hit the apple.
51672.m: Tell shot an apple off his son's head.

51673.q: According to the legend, which object on a pole were people in Altdorf supposed to greet?
51673.e: Gessler had his hat put on a pole in Altdorf. Everyone had to greet it, but Tell did not.
51673.m: Tell did not greet Gessler's hat.

51674.q: According to the legend, which weapon did Tell shoot with?
51674.e: Tell was a good shot with the crossbow. The monument in Altdorf also shows him with a crossbow.
51674.m: William Tell shot with a crossbow.

51675.q: Which play is performed in the Tell Theatre in Altdorf?
51675.e: Since 1899, amateur actors from Uri have performed Friedrich Schiller's play “William Tell” in Altdorf. Today they perform in the Tell Theatre.
51675.m: The play “William Tell” is performed in Altdorf.

51676.q: What material is the Tell Monument in Altdorf made of?
51676.e: The Tell Monument is cast in bronze. It was created by the sculptor Richard Kissling.
51676.m: The Tell Monument in Altdorf is made of bronze.

51677.q: Which famous monument stands on the village square of Altdorf?
51677.e: The Tell Monument in Altdorf shows William Tell with his son Walter. It was put up in 1895.
51677.m: The Tell Monument stands in Altdorf.

51678.q: Which place with a boat harbour on Lake Uri lies right next to Altdorf?
51678.e: Flüelen borders Altdorf to the north and lies on Lake Uri. The boats of Lake Lucerne stop there.
51678.m: Flüelen is the harbour town next to Altdorf.

51679.q: Which river flows through Lake Zug?
51679.e: The Lorze flows into the lake west of the town of Zug. Shortly afterwards it flows out again.
51679.m: The Lorze flows through Lake Zug.

51680.q: Which fish is a well-known speciality from Lake Zug?
51680.e: The Zug Rötel is a special kind of char. It lives in Lake Zug and is a popular fish to eat.
51680.m: The Zug Rötel is a fish from Lake Zug.

51681.q: Which three cantons border Lake Zug?
51681.e: Most of Lake Zug belongs to the canton of Zug. The south belongs to Schwyz and a small part to Lucerne.
51681.m: Lake Zug borders Zug, Schwyz and Lucerne.

51682.q: Which well-known mountain rises on the southern shore of Lake Zug?
51682.e: At the southern end of Lake Zug, the Rigi rises steeply. You can see the mountain well from the lake.
51682.m: The Rigi stands on the southern shore of Lake Zug.

51683.q: About how long is Lake Zug?
51683.e: Lake Zug is about 13.7 kilometres long. That is about 14 kilometres.
51683.m: Lake Zug is about 14 kilometres long.

51684.q: Which place lies at the southern end of Lake Zug?
51684.e: Arth lies in the canton of Schwyz at the southern end of the lake. The town of Zug, on the other hand, lies on the north-eastern shore.
51684.m: Arth lies at the southern end of Lake Zug.

51685.q: Near which place does the Lorze flow out of Lake Zug?
51685.e: The Lorze leaves Lake Zug near Cham. After that it flows on towards the Reuss.
51685.m: The Lorze flows out of Lake Zug near Cham.

51686.q: About how many kinds of fish live in Lake Zug?
51686.e: 32 kinds of fish live in Lake Zug. Important fish for eating are whitefish, perch and pike.
51686.m: About 30 kinds of fish live in Lake Zug.

51687.q: What are the two councils that debate laws in the Federal Palace called?
a: National Council and Council of States
51687.e: The National Council and the Council of States together form Parliament. They meet in two different halls in the Federal Palace.
51687.m: The National Council and the Council of States meet in the Federal Palace.

51688.q: Which bank has its head office right next to the Federal Palace on Federal Square?
51688.e: The Swiss National Bank has a large building on Federal Square. One of its jobs is looking after Switzerland's money.
51688.m: The National Bank stands on Federal Square next to the Federal Palace.

51689.q: How many water jets does the fountain on Federal Square have?
51689.e: On Federal Square, 26 jets of water shoot up out of the ground. Each jet stands for one canton.
51689.m: The 26 water jets on Federal Square stand for the 26 cantons.

51690.q: What takes place on Federal Square every Tuesday and Saturday?
51690.e: There is a market in front of the Federal Palace twice a week. You can buy vegetables, fruit and flowers there, for example.
51690.m: A market takes place in front of the Federal Palace twice a week.

51691.q: Which river flows past at the bottom of the slope behind the Federal Palace?
51691.e: The Federal Palace stands on a hill above the Aare. From the terrace you can look down at the river.
51691.m: The Aare flows past behind the Federal Palace.

51692.q: Which two chambers of Parliament meet in the Federal Palace?
a: National Council and Council of States
Federal Council and Federal Supreme Court
51692.e: The Swiss Parliament is called the Federal Assembly. It is made up of the National Council and the Council of States.
51692.m: The National Council and the Council of States meet in the Federal Palace.

51693.q: Which figures stand as a large statue in the domed hall of the Federal Palace?
51693.e: The statue shows the three men of the Rütli Oath. It is a reminder of the founding of the Swiss Confederation.
51693.m: In the domed hall, the three Confederates are a reminder of the Rütli Oath.

51694.q: What can you see in the glass dome inside the Federal Palace?
a: The coats of arms of the cantons
A large map of the world
51694.e: In the glass dome above the domed hall are the colourful coats of arms of the cantons. In the middle is the Swiss coat of arms.
51694.m: The coats of arms of the cantons shine in the glass dome of the Federal Palace.

51695.q: Which kind of bear lives in the Bear Park in Bern?
51695.e: Brown bears live in the Bear Park. These bears used to live in the forests of Switzerland too.
51695.m: Brown bears live in the Bear Park in Bern.

51696.q: What do the brown bears in the Bear Park eat?
51696.e: Brown bears are omnivores. They eat fruit, vegetables, nuts, fish and meat.
51696.m: Brown bears eat plants and meat.

51697.q: Why has the city of Bern kept bears for centuries?
a: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern
Bears protect the city from thieves
Bears are bred and sold there
Bears mow the grass on the banks of the Aare
51697.e: The bear is on the coat of arms of the city and the canton of Bern. Today the bears live in the Bear Park by the Aare.
51697.m: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern.

51698.q: Next to which bridge is the old Bear Pit in Bern?
51698.e: The Bear Pit lies at the end of the Old Town, just on the other side of the Nydegg Bridge.
51698.m: The old Bear Pit is near the Nydegg Bridge.

51699.q: Why was the Bear Park built in Bern?
a: To give the bears more space
51699.e: The bears had little space in the old round pit. In the Bear Park on the slope they can climb, dig and bathe.
51699.m: The bears have much more space in the Bear Park than in the old pit.

51700.q: What do the bears in the Bear Park usually do in winter?
51700.e: Brown bears sleep a lot in winter and hardly eat. This is called a winter rest.
51700.m: In winter, the bears have a winter rest.

51701.q: How long has Bern had bear pits?
51701.e: A first bear pit is known from as early as 1441. Since then it has been moved to a new place several times.
51701.m: Bern has kept bears for over 500 years.

51702.q: What does the old Bear Pit in Bern look like?
51702.e: The old Bear Pit is a deep, round pit with stone walls. Visitors look down into it from above.
51702.m: The old Bear Pit is a round pit with walls.

51703.q: Why has the city of Bern kept bears for so long?
a: The bear is its heraldic animal
51703.e: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern. That is why bears have lived in the city for a very long time.
51703.m: Bern keeps bears because the bear is its heraldic animal.

51704.q: Which figure on the Zytglogge rings two small bells?
51704.e: A jester with a jester's cap sits in a niche. Before the hour he rings two small bells above his head.
51704.m: A jester rings two small bells on the Zytglogge.

51705.q: What does the Bernese German word “Zytglogge” mean?
51705.e: In Bernese German, “Zyt” means time and “Glogge” means bell. The bell tells the time with its strokes.
51705.m: Zytglogge is Bernese German and means time bell.

51706.q: Which animal crows on the Zytglogge shortly before the hour?
51706.e: A wooden cockerel crows before every full hour. In this way it announces the show of figures.
51706.m: The cockerel on the Zytglogge crows before the hour.

51707.q: Which animals parade in a circle on the Zytglogge?
51707.e: Before the hour, a procession of little bear figures comes out of the tower. They carry weapons and musical instruments.
51707.m: A procession of bears goes past on the Zytglogge.

51708.q: Who strikes the hour with a hammer on the Zytglogge?
51708.e: Right at the top of the tower stands a gilded knight. He is called Hans von Thann and strikes the big bell with his hammer.
51708.m: A golden knight strikes the hours on the Zytglogge.

51709.q: About how old is the Zytglogge tower?
51709.e: The tower was built around 1218 to 1220. That makes it more than 800 years old.
51709.m: The Zytglogge is over 800 years old.

51710.q: What was the Zytglogge used for at the very beginning?
51710.e: At first the Zytglogge was a defensive tower on the western edge of the young city. It only got a clock later.
51710.m: The Zytglogge was first a tower to protect the city.

51711.q: How many minutes before the hour does the show of figures on the Zytglogge start?
51711.e: About four minutes before the hour, the figures start to move. That is why many tourists wait in front of the tower beforehand.
51711.m: The show of figures on the Zytglogge starts about four minutes before the hour.

51712.q: Which figure on the Zytglogge turns over an hourglass?
51712.e: Chronos is a bearded man and the god of time. He turns the hourglass and counts the strokes of the bell.
51712.m: Chronos, the god of time, turns over the hourglass on the Zytglogge.

51713.q: Which number is especially popular in the town of Solothurn?
51713.e: In Solothurn there are many things in elevens, for example churches, fountains and bells. That is why 11 is seen as the town's lucky number.
51713.m: The number 11 is Solothurn's favourite number.

51714.q: Which large church stands in the town of Solothurn?
51714.e: St Ursus Cathedral is the landmark of Solothurn. A wide staircase leads up to its entrance.
51714.m: St Ursus Cathedral is the large church of Solothurn.

51715.q: Which mountain lies to the north above the town of Solothurn?
51715.e: The Weissenstein is a mountain in the Jura. You can go up by gondola and look far out over the Swiss Plateau.
51715.m: The Weissenstein is Solothurn's local mountain.

51716.q: In which year did Solothurn join the Swiss Confederation?
51716.e: Solothurn was admitted to the Confederation in 1481 together with Fribourg. That made it the eleventh member.
51716.m: Solothurn has been part of the Confederation since 1481.

51717.q: What colours is the coat of arms of the canton of Solothurn?
51717.e: The coat of arms is red at the top and white at the bottom. It is very simple and has no animal.
51717.m: The Solothurn coat of arms is red and white.

51718.q: Which language do most people in the canton of Solothurn speak?
51718.e: The canton of Solothurn is in German-speaking Switzerland. In everyday life people speak Swiss German.
51718.m: German is spoken in the canton of Solothurn.

51719.q: Which town is also called the “Town of Ambassadors”?
51719.e: For a long time, the ambassadors of the King of France lived in Solothurn. That is how it got its nickname.
51719.m: Solothurn is called the Town of Ambassadors because French ambassadors used to live there.

51720.q: Since which year has Aargau been a canton of its own?
51720.e: The canton of Aargau was founded in 1803. Before that, its lands belonged to various rulers.
51720.m: Aargau has been a canton since 1803.

51721.q: Why is Aargau also called the “canton of castles”?
a: It lies high in the mountains
51721.e: There are many castles in Aargau, for example Lenzburg, Hallwyl and Wildegg.
51721.m: Aargau is the canton of castles.

51722.q: Which castle in Aargau gave its name to a famous ruling family?
51722.e: The Habsburg family comes from Habsburg Castle near Brugg. Later they became emperors in Austria.
51722.m: The Habsburgs got their name from Habsburg Castle in Aargau.

51723.q: What was the large Roman camp near Windisch in Aargau called?
51723.e: Around 2000 years ago, there was a large camp of Roman soldiers near Windisch. It was called Vindonissa.
51723.m: The Roman camp of Vindonissa was near Windisch in Aargau.

51724.q: Which canton borders Aargau to the east?
51724.e: The canton of Zurich lies to the east of Aargau. Solothurn and Basel-Landschaft border it to the west.
51724.m: The canton of Zurich is Aargau's eastern neighbour.

51725.q: Which vegetable is in Aargau's nickname “Rüebliland”?
51725.e: In the past, a particularly large number of carrots were grown in Aargau. In Switzerland, carrots are also called Rüebli.
51725.m: Aargau is also called Rüebliland because of its carrots.

51726.q: Which large river forms the border between Aargau and Germany in the north?
51726.e: The Rhine flows along the north of Aargau. Germany lies on the other side.
51726.m: The Rhine separates Aargau from Germany.
